name: Chengdu
tagline: Laid-Back Megacity of Pandas and Teahouses
description: Chengdu is a laid-back, food-famous Sichuan megacity offering a high quality of life well below China's coastal costs — pandas, teahouses, spicy cuisine, and an excellent modern metro. The tradeoffs are real: a language barrier, the Great Firewall, and a near-impossible long-stay visa path for non-working retirees.

quickFacts.visa: No retirement or digital-nomad visa; long-stay essentially requires employment (Z), family ties (Q/S), or major investment; most non-working retirees cannot legally settle long-term, and an HIV test is required for residence permits
quickFacts.internetSpeed: Fast and cheap domestically, but a VPN is needed for foreign sites (Great Firewall)
quickFacts.safetyRating: Very safe with low violent crime; air pollution is the main health caveat

dining.description: Cheap local restaurants (¥20–50/meal) and home cooking

entertainment.description: Teahouses, parks, and the panda base

1M.lifestyle: A modern-ish outer-district 1BR, eating cheaply at local restaurants and cooking at home, getting around by metro and e-bike, and relying on basic local care. A VPN handles home internet. Genuinely comfortable by local standards on very little.

dining.description: Frequent dining out across Chengdu's famous food scene

entertainment.description: People's Park nightlife, teahouses, and an active social life

2M.lifestyle: A central flat near People's Park nightlife, frequent dining in one of China's best food cities, basic international insurance, and an active social life — comfortable urban living at a fraction of coastal cost.

housing.description: Modern 2–3BR in Tianfu or central Chengdu

transportation.description: Ride-hailing and the occasional domestic flight

3M.lifestyle: A spacious modern apartment, frequent quality dining, international insurance, and domestic travel define a comfortable expat life — provided the visa and language barriers are surmountable.

housing.description: Luxury serviced apartment in the center

5M.lifestyle: A serviced luxury apartment, near-daily dining, a part-time ayi, and VIP international-clinic care. Premium urban living with frequent travel, well below the cost of China's tier-1 coastal cities.

dining.description: Private-chef dining and the finest restaurants

entertainment.description: Elite clubs, luxury travel, and a full social scene

10M.lifestyle: A penthouse, full domestic staff, a private driver, and concierge international healthcare. Fine dining and luxury travel make this Fat-FIRE living for a fraction of Western or coastal-China cost.
